Art. 9.title: Risk Management System
Art. 9.description: High-risk AI systems shall have a risk management system established, implemented, documented and maintained. The system shall identify and analyse known and reasonably foreseeable risks, estimate and evaluate risks that may emerge, and adopt appropriate risk management measures.

Art. 10.title: Data and Data Governance
Art. 10.description: High-risk AI systems using techniques involving training with data shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet quality criteria. Data governance and management practices shall address relevant design choices, data collection processes, and examination for biases.

Art. 12.title: Record-Keeping
Art. 12.description: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for automatic recording of events (logs) over their lifetime. Logging capabilities shall ensure traceability of the AI system's functioning, enabling monitoring and post-market surveillance.

Art. 13.title: Transparency and Provision of Information
Art. 13.description: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed to ensure their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret a system's output and use it appropriately. Users shall be provided with concise, complete, correct and clear information.

Art. 14.title: Human Oversight
Art. 14.description: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed to be effectively overseen by natural persons during use. Human oversight shall aim to prevent or minimise risks to health, safety or fundamental rights that may emerge when a high-risk AI system is used in accordance with its intended purpose.

Art. 15.title: Accuracy, Robustness and Cybersecurity
Art. 15.description: High-risk AI systems shall achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity, and perform consistently in those respects throughout their lifecycle. They shall be resilient against attempts by unauthorised third parties to alter their use, outputs or performance.

Art. 21.title: Cybersecurity Risk-Management Measures
Art. 21.description: Essential and important entities shall take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage risks posed to the security of network and information systems. Measures shall include risk analysis policies, incident handling, business continuity, supply chain security, and access control policies.

Art. 23.title: Reporting Obligations
Art. 23.description: Essential and important entities shall notify significant incidents to the competent authority or CSIRT. Early warning within 24 hours, incident notification within 72 hours, and final report within one month. Reports shall include incident assessment, severity, impact, and any cross-border effects.

Art. 6.title: ICT Risk Management Framework
Art. 6.description: Financial entities shall have a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework as part of their overall risk management system. The framework shall include strategies, policies, procedures, ICT protocols and tools necessary to protect information and ICT assets.

Art. 6 to 8.title: ICT Risk Management Framework
Art. 6 to 8.description: Financial entities shall have a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework (Art. 6), use and maintain updated ICT systems appropriate to support operations (Art. 7), and identify, classify and document all ICT-supported business functions, information assets and their dependencies (Art. 8).

Art. 6 to 9.title: ICT Risk Management Framework and Protection
Art. 6 to 9.description: Comprehensive ICT risk management requirements: establishing the framework (Art. 6), maintaining ICT systems (Art. 7), identification and classification (Art. 8), and protection and prevention measures including access management, identity management, and continuous monitoring (Art. 9).

Art. 9.title: Protection and Prevention
Art. 9.description: Financial entities shall continuously monitor and control the security and functioning of ICT systems, minimise the impact of ICT risk through resilient systems, and implement policies limiting access to ICT assets based on the principle of least privilege.

Art. 12.title: Backup Policies and Recovery
Art. 12.description: Financial entities shall maintain backup policies and procedures, determine recovery time and point objectives, and ensure the ability to restore systems from backups. Backup systems shall be geographically separated from main processing sites.

Art. 17 to 19.title: ICT Incident Management and Reporting
Art. 17 to 19.description: Financial entities shall establish incident management processes (Art. 17), classify incidents based on severity criteria including affected clients, duration, and economic impact (Art. 18), and report major incidents within 4 hours initial notification, 72 hours intermediate report, and one month final report (Art. 19).

Art. 28 to 30.title: ICT Third-Party Risk
Art. 28 to 30.description: Financial entities shall manage ICT third-party risk as integral to their ICT risk framework (Art. 28), maintain a register of all ICT third-party providers (Art. 29), and ensure contracts include mandatory provisions on service levels, data location, audit rights, and termination (Art. 30).

Art. 5(1)(b).title: Purpose Limitation
Art. 5(1)(b).description: Personal data shall be collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not further processed in a manner incompatible with those purposes.

Art. 5(1)(c).title: Data Minimisation
Art. 5(1)(c).description: Personal data shall be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary in relation to the purposes for which they are processed.

Art. 5(1)(d).title: Accuracy
Art. 5(1)(d).description: Personal data shall be accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date. Every reasonable step must be taken to ensure that inaccurate data are erased or rectified without delay.

Art. 5(1)(f).title: Integrity and Confidentiality
Art. 5(1)(f).description: Personal data shall be processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage, using appropriate technical or organisational measures.

Art. 5(2).title: Accountability
Art. 5(2).description: The controller shall be responsible for, and be able to demonstrate compliance with, the data protection principles (lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality).

Art. 17.title: Right to Erasure
Art. 17.description: The data subject shall have the right to obtain from the controller the erasure of personal data concerning them without undue delay where certain grounds apply, including where data is no longer necessary or consent is withdrawn.

Art. 22.title: Automated Individual Decision-Making
Art. 22.description: Data subjects have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects them. Exceptions require explicit consent, contractual necessity, or legal authorisation with suitable safeguards.

Art. 25.title: Data Protection by Design and Default
Art. 25.description: Controllers shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures designed to implement data protection principles effectively and integrate necessary safeguards into processing. By default, only personal data necessary for each specific purpose shall be processed.

Art. 30.title: Records of Processing Activities
Art. 30.description: Controllers and processors shall maintain written records of processing activities including purposes, categories of data subjects and data, recipients, transfers to third countries, retention periods, and a description of technical and organisational security measures.

Art. 32.title: Security of Processing
Art. 32.description: Controllers and processors shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk, including pseudonymisation, encryption, ensuring confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience, restoration capability, and regular testing.
